claims.text: The onset and progression of the premelting/melting transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles is controlled by enhanced surface atomic mobility.
Enhanced surface atomic mobility nucleates a liquid-like surface layer before bulk melting.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are solid and crystalline with well-defined surfaces.
Surface passivation provides a controlled perturbation of the proposed surface-mobility mechanism.
Increased surface atomic diffusion produces a disordered, liquid-like surface layer.
At elevated temperatures, surface atoms have greater thermal vibrations than bulk atoms because they have lower coordination and binding energies.
Thermally induced surface disorder enhances surface diffusion.
Enhanced surface diffusion nucleates a transient liquid-like phase.
The liquid-like phase propagates inward as temperature increases.
Unpassivated nanoparticles will develop surface disorder and a detectable liquid-like layer below the bulk melting point.
Passivated nanoparticles will undergo surface transformation at a higher temperature than unpassivated nanoparticles.
Surface-atom diffusion rates will increase significantly before bulk melting.
At room temperature, the baseline nanoparticles have a uniform crystalline structure without surface disorder.
The proposed surface-mobility-controlled behavior is expected under high vacuum and controlled heating rates.
Impurities may alter the nanoparticles' thermal-transition behavior and diffusion dynamics.
Non-uniform particle sizes may alter diffusion dynamics and shift the transition-onset temperature.
Bulk thermal expansion may contribute alongside surface diffusion to the observed transition.
Failure to observe earlier or stronger surface disorder in unpassivated particles, or failure to observe enhanced surface diffusion before bulk melting, would falsify the hypothesis.
